args.summary: The party arranged a daylight passage with Sela Thorn, explored Saltmere Mine and found a hymn page marked "M. Brand", then witnessed the drowned bell and submerged congregation at midnight. At the Tarred Gull they planned a daylight dive for tomorrow; Bram offered a different account of Maren. The Hollow Choir clock reached three of six.

properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at pier four
properties.played_as: Whispers as though the water might hear her; avoids eye contact and watches the tide line. Grey braid and salt-stained coat.
properties.wants: Offers to row the party by day for two silver; refuses night passage.
properties.knows: Says Saltmere flooded forty years ago, the night the bell first rang; her grandmother said the rising water was warm.

sources.quote: She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
Fine, she'll do it for two silver.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: The party met and negotiated passage with a new NPC.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: Sela was encountered at the docks.

properties.statement: Sela says Saltmere flooded forty years ago on the night the bell first rang; she reports her grandmother's claim that the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Records an attributed historical claim without confirming its timing or cause.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: The historical claim concerns Saltmere Mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. Black entrance in chalk, half-rotted timber frame and overturned rusted cart. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces inside, warm black water floods the tunnel; wet hymn-book pages float and cling to the walls.
properties.state: Closed; tunnel flooded thirty paces inside with warm black water.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: The party explored the previously known mine and observed its condition.

properties.statement: A wet hymn-book page retrieved from Saltmere Mine contains a hymn about the sea giving back what it takes and the pencilled marginal inscription "M. Brand".

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Records the observed clue without confirming who wrote it.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Locates the physical clue at the mine.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. A hymn page found in Saltmere Mine bears "M. Brand"; Teo believes it is Mira's handwriting and evidence she was there.

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: The clue advances Teo's search while his identification remains a player interpretation.

change.name: Is Maren involved in the choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is in a cult and Oren suspects she runs the choir. These are unconfirmed player guesses.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Keeps player suspicion as an open question rather than an NPC fact.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.

changes.why: Identifies the subject of the players' suspicion.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water, the roof, bell tower and two broken arches protrude; seaweed hangs from the stones.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.

changes.why: Adds the party's first direct view of the chapel.

properties.role: One of two fishermen hauling their boat ashore below the chapel
properties.played_as: Warns the party not to stand close to the water and invokes the Kelp Mother as something everyone knows; voice and physical manner were not recorded.
properties.knows: Repeats the local claim that the Kelp Mother pulls children into the water by their ankles.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
Two fishermen hauling their boat up. One of them sees you looking at the water.

changes.why: Records the voiced fisherman without assigning Speaker 1 to Sela or inventing a performance.

sources.quote: You get back to Gullwick by dusk, and you decide to go down to the shore below the old chapel ruins anyway, Sela's warning or not.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Places the fisherman on the shore below the chapel before he leaves.

properties.what_is_open: A fisherman claims the Kelp Mother pulls children into the water by their ankles. Oren asked whether it is real; the GM only attributed the story to the fishermen.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Keeps the local warning unresolved rather than creating a confirmed creature.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.

changes.why: Identifies the warning's source.

change.name: Midnight shapes in the drowned chapel

properties.statement: At midnight the submerged bell rang twelve times with stronger humming; pale shapes stood in rows on the chapel floor like a congregation and vanished when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.
And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.

changes.why: Records the observed apparition without identifying what the shapes are.

sources.quote: Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Locates the apparition in the drowned chapel.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the submerged bell? It rang twelve times at midnight again with louder humming; pale congregation-like shapes appeared on the chapel floor and vanished when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.
And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.

changes.why: The party gained direct evidence but the bell's ringer remains unknown.

sources.quote: That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: The GM explicitly advanced the existing hidden story clock.

properties.details_shown: Tavern and inn by the docks; fire burning, smell of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
Long rest at the inn?
Yes, long rest, you're all back to full. And that's where we stop for tonight.

changes.why: Records the party's end-of-session location.

properties.played_as: Huge, red-bearded; laughs at his own jokes and continually wipes the same mug. Calls the party brave or stupid and gives them stew on the house.
properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued with a good heart, and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Records the new voiced innkeeper and his account of Maren.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Bram works at the tavern where the party met him.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: Records Bram's last observed location.

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects Maren is in a cult and Oren suspects she runs the choir, without confirmation. Bram says he has known her thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued with a good heart, and says she lost a brother to the bay. Her involvement remains unresolved.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Adds attributed testimony relevant to the suspicion without settling it.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Preserves the source of the countervailing account.

properties.next_step: The party plans to meet Sela at pier four tomorrow at first light for passage, then dive to the chapel at low tide during daylight; Vessa intends to buy rope and a second lantern tonight.

sources.quote: So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Records the declared plan without treating the passage, dive or purchases as completed.

properties.what_changed: Mira heard the bell the night she left. A hymn page at Saltmere Mine bears "M. Brand", which Teo believes is Mira's handwriting. He believes the hymns came from the chapel and plans to pursue that lead in tomorrow's daylight dive.

sources.quote: Okay, plan. Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Records Teo's interpretation and chosen lead as progress on his goal.

changes.why: The party ended the session at the inn.
